prompt: Implement the Builder pattern: Pizza has a private constructor and is created only through its nested Builder with a required size and optional cheese and toppings. Complete the Builder and the describe method.
explanation: The Builder pattern replaces a long constructor with readable chained calls: required values go in the Builder's constructor, optional ones become methods that set a field and return this so calls can be chained. Because Pizza's constructor is private, build() is the only way to create one, and the Pizza itself stays immutable (all fields final). Each optional method returning this is what makes the fluent chain work.
hints: Give the Builder its own fields: a final String size set in its constructor, a boolean cheese, and a List<String> toppings initialized to an empty ArrayList.
cheese() and addTopping(...) mutate the Builder's fields and return this -- that is what enables chaining.
build() simply calls the private Pizza constructor with the three collected values; describe() then branches on the cheese flag and toppings.size().
